source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p17 net long-term capital gains and Line 2; PDF p18 net long-term capital gains rate tables; Form 2 PDF p2 lines 1-13; record capital_gains

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + interest 5,000.00 + dividends 10,000.00 + short-term gains 5,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 34,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 34,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 34,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 34,250.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 34,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 34,250.00 = 2,020.75, less 253 = 1,767.75; line 13 = 1,767.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (34,250.00 - 21,100.00 = 13,150.00) = 775.85; bracket tax 1,767.55. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,767.55. The form gives 1,767.75; expected keeps the projection's 1,767.55, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). Montana ordinary income is all taxable income that is not a net long-term capital gain and includes qualified dividends (PDF p17); short-term gains and interest are ordinary too, so none of this pays a gains rate.
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
